**Surah Hud**

Makkan, except for His saying: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾. It has one hundred and twenty-three verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book﴾, meaning: this is a Book. ﴿Its verses have been made firm﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was not abrogated (naskh) by another Book, as the earlier scriptures and laws were abrogated by it. ﴿Then they have been detailed﴾, meaning: they have been explained with the rulings, and with what is lawful (halal) and what is unlawful (haram). Al-Hasan said: they were made firm through command and prohibition, then detailed through promise and threat. Qatadah said: they were made firm, meaning Allah made them firm, so there is in them no contradiction and no inconsistency. Mujahid said: ﴿detailed﴾ means explained (tafsir). It was also said: ﴿detailed﴾ means that it was sent down piece by piece. ﴿From One who is Wise and All-Aware﴾.

﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾, meaning: and in that Book is: that you worship none but Allah. The place of "an" (that) is in the nominative case. It was also said that its place is in the genitive case, its implied sense being: "with [the message] that you worship none but Allah". ﴿Indeed I am to you from Him﴾, meaning from Allah, ﴿a warner﴾ to the disobedient, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ to the obedient.

﴿And that﴾ is conjoined to the first, ﴿ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾, meaning: return to Him in obedience. Al-Farra' said: "then" (thumma) here has the meaning of "and" (wa), meaning: "and turn to Him in repentance", because seeking forgiveness is repentance and repentance is seeking forgiveness.

It was also said: "that ask forgiveness of your Lord [from the sins] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] then turn to Him" in the future [[In "B": "the future (al-mustaqbal)".]].

﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾, meaning He will let you live a good life [[The bracketed text in the source reads: "a good life in ease, tranquility, safety and abundance". Manuscript "B" reads: "in abundance, tranquility and safety".]]. Some of them said: the good life is contentment with what is easy and patience with what is decreed.

﴿Until a specified term﴾, meaning until the time of death. ﴿And He will give every person of merit his merit﴾, meaning: He will give every person of good deeds his reward and recompense in the Hereafter for his good deeds in this world. Abu al-'Aliyah said: whoever's obedience increases in this world, his ranks in the Hereafter increase [[in Paradise]] [[Omitted in "B".]], because ranks are determined by deeds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds enters Paradise, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds enters the Fire, and whoever's good and bad deeds are equal is among the People of the Heights (al-A'raf), then enters Paradise afterward [[Addition from "B".]].

It was also said: "And He will give every person of merit his merit" means: whoever acts for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will grant him success in what is to come, in His obedience.

﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: they turn away, ﴿then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 4–5:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Behold, they fold up their breasts﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. (306), and al-Qurtubi: 9 / 5.]] It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq, who was a man sweet of speech and sweet of appearance, who would meet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with what he loved, while concealing in his heart what he hated.

His saying "they fold up their breasts" means: they conceal what is in their breasts of rancour and enmity. [[In "B": "they gather".]]

ʿAbdullah ibn Shaddad said: It was revealed concerning some of the hypocrites who, when they passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would bend their chest and back, lower their heads, and cover their faces so that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not see them. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15 / 233–234.]]

Qatadah said: They would bend their chests so that they would not hear the Book of Allah the Exalted or His remembrance. [[In "B": "speech".]] [[See: al-Tabari: 15 / 235.]]

It has also been said: A man among the disbelievers would enter his house, let down his curtain, bend his back, wrap himself in his garment, and say: "Does Allah know what is in my heart?"

As-Suddi said: "yathnuna" means they turn away with their hearts, from their saying: "I turned my rein" (thaniytu ʿinani). It is also said: they incline, and from it comes "thaniy al-thawb" (the folding of a garment).

Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "yathnawni" [[In al-Tabari: "tathnuni" with a upper tā', on the pattern of "tahlawli al-thamara" and "tafʿawʿal".]] on the pattern of "yahlawli", making the verb act as a verbal noun, and its meaning is intensification of folding.

﴿That they may hide from Him﴾: that is, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Mujahid said: that they may hide from Allah, if they are able. ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾: they cover their heads with their garments. ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they reveal; indeed He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾. Al-Azhari said: The meaning of the verse from beginning to end is that those who harbour enmity toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), their condition is not hidden from us.

Abdul-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Hasan [[In "B": "al-Husayn", and likewise in al-Tabari; the text here follows "A", which is also the reading in al-Bukhari.]] ibn Muhammad ibn Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Jaʿfar informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, recite: ﴿Behold, they fold up their breasts﴾. He said: I asked him about it, and he said: Some people were shy to relieve themselves in the open lest they expose themselves to the sky, and shy to have intercourse with their wives lest they expose themselves to the sky, so this was revealed concerning them. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter: "Behold, they fold up their breasts..." 8 / 349. See also al-Tabari: 15 / 236–237.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth⦆ meaning: there is no creature, the "min" (min) being extra (ṣilah). And al-dābbah (the creature that moves): every living being that crawls upon the face of the earth.

His saying ﴿but its provision is upon Allah﴾ meaning: He is the one who undertakes that out of bounty, and it is subject to His will: if He wills, He provides, and if He wills, He does not provide.

It was also said: "ʿalā" (upon) is in the sense of "min" (from), meaning: its provision is from Allah.

Mujahid said: whatever provision comes to it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and at times He does not provide for it until it dies of hunger.

﴿And He knows its resting place and its place of storage﴾. Ibn Miqsam said: and this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "its resting place" is the place where it takes refuge and settles by night and by day, and "its place of storage" is the place where it is buried when it dies.

ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "the resting place" is the wombs of the mothers, and "the place of storage" [the place where it dies] [in "B": (the loins of the fathers)]. [And ʿAta said: the resting place is the wombs of the mothers, and the place of storage is the loins of the fathers] [omitted from "B"].

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, and ʿIkrimah also related this from Ibn ʿAbbas. [The view preferred by al-Tabari is that His saying "and He knows its resting place" refers to where it settles, which is its refuge where it takes shelter by night or by day, "and its place of storage" refers to the place where it is deposited, either by its death there or its burial... because Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed that whatever provision the creatures receive is from Him, so it is more fitting that this should be followed by the statement that He knows their abode and resting place, rather than information about His knowledge of what the loins and wombs contain.]

It was also said: the resting place is Paradise or Hell, and the place of storage is the grave, based on His saying, exalted is He, describing Paradise and Hell: ﴿Excellent as a place of rest and as a station﴾ [al-Furqan: 76].

﴿All is in a Clear Book﴾ meaning: all is recorded in the Preserved Tablet before He created it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water﴾ — before He created [the heaven and the earth] [[In "B": (the heaven).]]. That water was upon the back of the wind [[This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-Tabari 15/349, and in al-Tarikh likewise 1/21. al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak 2/341, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]].

Ka'b [[Ka'b al-Ahbar is among the transmitters of the Isra'iliyyat, and we have not found anyone other than him mention this.]] said: Allah, mighty and majestic, created a green ruby, then He looked at it with awe, and it became water trembling. Then He created the wind, and placed the water upon its back. Then He set the Throne upon the water.

Damrah said: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, His Throne was upon the water, then He created the heavens and the earth, and He created the Pen, and it wrote with it what He would create and what would come to be from His creation. Then that Book glorified Allah and extolled Him for a thousand years before He created anything of His creation [[Narrated by al-Tabari 15/249. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, cited some hadiths in explaining this verse, among them the hadith of Imam Ahmad and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from 'Imran ibn Husayn, in which: "Allah was, and nothing was before Him" — in one narration: "besides Him," and in another: "with Him" — "and His Throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Reminder everything, then He created the heavens and the earth." In Sahih Muslim from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah decreed the measures of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was upon the water." Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from Luqayt ibn 'Amir, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created His creation?" He said: "He was in 'ama' (a cloud), with nothing beneath it and nothing above it air; then He created the Throne after that." See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/438.]]

﴿That He may test you﴾ — to examine you, though He is most knowing — ﴿which of you is best in deed﴾: the one who is most diligent in obedience to Allah and most scrupulous in avoiding the prohibitions of Allah, exalted is He.

﴿And if you say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Indeed you will be resurrected after death,"﴾ — that is, ﴿the disbelievers will surely say, "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ They mean the Qur'an.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited: "sahir" (a magician), meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 8–9:

﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted nation﴾ — until a specified term. The root of ʾummah (ummah, a community or group) is "a group," so it is as if He said: until the extinction of one community and the coming of another community. ﴿they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ — i.e., "What is it that is holding it back?" They say this out of haste for the punishment and in mockery, meaning: it is nothing at all.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them﴾ — meaning the punishment; it will not be turned away from them. ﴿And there will surround them﴾ — it will descend upon them, ﴿that which they used to mock﴾ — i.e., the consequence of their mockery.

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ — a blessing and abundance, ﴿then We withdraw it from him﴾ — i.e., We strip it away from him, ﴿indeed, he is despairing﴾ — despairing (qunut) in hardship, ﴿ungrateful﴾ — for the blessing.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 10–12:

﴿And if We give man a taste of favor after adversity has touched him﴾ after a trial that befell him, ﴿he will surely say, "Gone are the evils from me,"﴾ meaning the hardships have departed from me, ﴿indeed, he is exultant and boastful﴾ insolent and arrogant. Al-farah (joy) is a pleasure in the heart at attaining what is desired, and al-fakhr (boasting) is to show superiority over people by enumerating one's virtues, and that is forbidden.

﴿Except those who are patient﴾ Al-Farra' said: this is an exceptive clause of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), meaning: "But those who are patient." ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ for indeed, if hardship reaches them, they are patient, and if they attain a blessing, they are thankful. ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾ for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾ which is Paradise.

﴿So perhaps you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿would leave some of what is revealed to you﴾ and not convey it to them. That is because the disbelievers of Makkah, when they said, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it" [Yunus: 15], meaning one that does not revile our gods, the Prophet ﷺ intended to leave their gods alone openly, so Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿So perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you﴾ [[See: al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn 'Atiyyah: 7/249 – after mentioning the occasion of revelation he said: "Allah the Exalted addressed His Prophet ﷺ in this form of address, confronting him with it, refuting their statements and nullifying them. The meaning is not that he ﷺ intended something of this and was then rebuked for it, for he never intended to leave any part of what was revealed to him, nor did his chest constrict; rather his chest would constrict over their statements and actions and their distance from faith." Then he said after that: "... It is possible that the Prophet ﷺ found the hardship he encountered very grave, so he inclined toward wishing that Allah grant permission for some leniency toward the disbelievers, and similar beliefs that befit him ﷺ, as the verses of conciliation came with." ]] i.e., the reviling of the gods. ﴿And your chest would be constricted thereby﴾ meaning: perhaps your chest would become constricted ﴿that they say﴾ i.e., because they say, ﴿"Why has not a treasure been sent down to him,"﴾ which he would spend, ﴿or an angel come with him?"﴾ who would confirm him. This was said by Abdullah ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ it is not incumbent upon you except conveyance, ﴿and Allah is Disposer of all things﴾ Guardian.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 16–17:

﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein [i.e., in the world] is nullified, and what they used to do is void.﴾

They differed concerning the meaning of this verse. Mujahid said: They are the people of showing off (riya').  It has been related to us that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, what I fear most for you is the minor shirk (ash-shirk al-asghar)." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the minor shirk?" He said: "Showing off (ar-riya')."

It has been said: This refers to the disbelievers. As for the believer, he desires both the world and the Hereafter, but his desire for the Hereafter predominates, so he is rewarded for his good deeds in this world and is recompensed for them in the Hereafter.

It has been related to us from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not wrong a believer in a good deed: he is given provision for it in this world, and is repaid for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for his good deeds in this world, until when he reaches the Hereafter he has no good deed for which he is given any reward."

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Is then one who is upon clear evidence (bayyinah)﴾ from his Lord — it has been said: there is an ellipsis in the verse, and its meaning is: "Is then one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one who desires the worldly life and its adornment," or "one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one who is in error and ignorance." And what is meant by "the one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord" is the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿And a witness from Him recites it﴾ — that is, one follows him who testifies to his truthfulness. They differed concerning this witness. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Alqamah, Ibrahim, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, and most of the people of tafsir (tafsir: exegesis) said: it is Jibril, peace be upon him.

al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid that he said: it is an angel who protects him and guides him.

al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the Qur'an, its composition and its inimitability.

It has also been said: it is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. 'Ali said: "There is no man from Quraysh except that a verse of the Qur'an was revealed concerning him." A man said to him: "And what was revealed concerning you?" He said: ﴿And a witness from Him recites it﴾.

It has been said: the "witness from Him" is the Injil (Gospel).

﴿And before it﴾ — that is, before the coming of Muhammad ﷺ. It has also been said: before the revelation of the Qur'an.

﴿The Book of Musa﴾ — that is, the Book of Musa was ﴿a leader and a mercy﴾ for those who followed it, meaning the Torah, which confirms the Qur'an and bears witness to the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿Those believe in it﴾ — meaning the companions of Muhammad ﷺ. It has also been said: it refers to those among the People of the Book who embraced Islam.

﴿And whoever disbelieves in it﴾ — that is, in Muhammad ﷺ. It has also been said: in the Qur'an, ﴿among the factions﴾ — among the disbelievers from the people of all the religions — ﴿the Fire is his promised place.﴾

Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us; Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, related to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one from this community hears of me, nor any Jew or Christian, then dies without having believed in what I have been sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾ — that is, do not be in doubt about it — ﴿indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.﴾

﴿And who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ So he claims that He has a son or a partner. That is, there is no one more wrong than him. ﴿Those﴾, meaning the liars and the deniers, ﴿will be presented before their Lord﴾, and He will question them about their deeds.

﴿And the witnesses will say﴾, meaning the angels who used to record their deeds. This is the view of Mujahid [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/283; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/412-413.]].

It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that they are the prophets and messengers, peace and blessings be upon them. This is also the view of al-Dahhak [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/283; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/412-413.]].

Qatadah said: they are all of creation.

It has also been related to us from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will bring the believer near, place His veil (kanaf) over him and conceal him, then say: 'Do you recognize the sin of such-and-such? Do you recognize the sin of such-and-such?' He will say: 'Yes, my Lord.' Until, when He has made him acknowledge his sins and he sees in himself that he is ruined, He will say: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' Then he will be given the book of his good deeds." As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, [they will be called out before the heads of all creation] [[In "B": "fa-yaqulu al-ashhad" (then the witnesses will say), and the version adopted from "A" is the one that agrees with the narration of al-Bukhari.]], "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, chapter on the saying of Allah, "Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers," 5/96, and in al-Tawhid and al-Riqaq. Related by Muslim in al-Tawbah, chapter on the acceptance of the repentance of a killer even if his killings were many, no. 2766: 4/2120. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/132-133. His words in the hadith, "fa-yada'u 'alayhi kanafahu," with a fatha on the kaf and the nun, followed by a fa', where kanaf means the veil or covering. This is explained in that way in the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Muhammad ibn Sawa from Qatadah, where at the end of the hadith he says: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: "kanafahu" means "sitrahu" (his covering). Related by al-Bukhari in Khalq Af'al al-Ibad. The meaning is that he is enveloped by complete care. Whoever narrates it with a kasra on the ta' (kitfahu, "his shoulder") has made an error, as a group of scholars have firmly held. See: Fath al-Bari: 13/477.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 19–22:

﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah﴾ — they prevent (people) from the religion of Allah, ﴿and seek to make it crooked, and they are, of the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾.

﴿They were not ones who could escape⁠﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "outrunning" (sabiqin). Qatadah said: "fleeing" (haribin). Muqatil said: "escaping" (fa'itin).

﴿in the earth, and they had no protectors besides Allah﴾ — meaning: helpers and supporters who would guard them from Our punishment. ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾ — i.e., their punishment will be increased. It has been said: the punishment will be doubled for them because they led others astray and because the followers imitated them.

﴿They could not hear, nor did they see﴾ — Qatadah said: deaf to hearing the truth, so they do not hear it, and they did not see the guidance. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He prevented the people of polytheism from obeying Him in this world and the Hereafter. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 23–26:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds and humbled themselves﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They feared." Qatadah said: "They turned in repentance." Mujahid said: "They were at ease." It was also said: "They were humble." His saying ﴿to their Lord﴾ means "for their Lord."

﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿The likeness of the two groups﴾, the believer and the disbeliever, ﴿is like the blind and the deaf and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then will you not be reminded?﴾ Al-Farra' said: "He did not say hal yastawūn (هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ), because the blind and the deaf are in one category, as if they were one, since they are both descriptions of the disbeliever. And the seeing and the hearing are in one category, as if they were one, since they are both descriptions of the believer." ﴿Then will you not be reminded?﴾ means: "Will you not take admonition?"

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner."﴾ Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read "annī" (أَنِّي) with a fatha on the hamzah, meaning "that I," and the rest read it with a kasra, meaning "so he said, indeed I," because sending carries the sense of saying: "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner."

﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.﴾ That is, "painful" (mu'lim). Ibn ʿAbbas said: Noah, peace be upon him, was sent after forty years, and he remained calling his people nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived after the Flood sixty years, and his lifespan was one thousand and fifty years.

Muqatil said: He was sent when he was one hundred years old.

It was said: He was sent when he was fifty years old.

It was also said: He was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old, and he remained calling his people nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived after the Flood two hundred and fifty years, so his lifespan was one thousand four hundred and fifty years. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 14], meaning: he remained among them as a caller.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 27–29:

﴿Then said the chiefs who disbelieved among his people﴾. Al-mala' are the nobles and the leaders.

﴿And we see you﴾, O Noah, ﴿only a human being﴾ like us, ﴿like us. And we see that none follow you except those who are our lowly ones﴾, our meanest. Al-radhl means the base of everything, and its plural is arudh, then it is pluralized as arathil, like kalb (dog), aklub, and akalib. In Surat ash-Shu'ara' He said: "And those who follow you are the lowest," meaning the meanest. Ikrimah said: the weavers and the cobblers. ﴿Immature opinion﴾: Abu 'Amr read "bade" with a hamza (ba'i'), meaning the first opinion, meaning they followed you at first thought without reflection and contemplation, and had they reflected they would not have followed you. The others read it without a hamza, meaning apparent opinion, from their saying: "badā al-shay'" when it appeared, meaning: they followed you outwardly without examining and contemplating inwardly. Mujahid said: the opinion of the eye (apparent sight). ﴿And we do not see that you have any merit over us; rather we think you are liars﴾.

﴿He said﴾, Noah: ﴿O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾, meaning: a clear explanation from my Lord, ﴿and He has given me mercy﴾, meaning: guidance and knowledge, ﴿from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you﴾, meaning: it has been hidden from you and confused for you. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read "fa-'ummiyat 'alaykum" with a dammah on the ayn and a shaddah on the mim, meaning: it has been made to look dubious and confused upon you.

﴿Shall we compel you to it﴾, meaning: shall we compel you to the evidence and the mercy, ﴿while you are averse to it﴾, not desiring it. Qatadah said: If the prophets, upon them be blessings and peace, had been able to compel their people to faith, they would have compelled them, but they were not able to.

His saying: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it﴾, meaning: for the revelation and conveying the message, as a figure of speech for what is not mentioned, ﴿my reward is not but from Allah. And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾. This is evidence that they asked him to drive away the believers. ﴿Indeed, they are meeting their Lord﴾, meaning: they will return to their Lord in the Hereafter, and He will recompense whoever drove them away. ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾

﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon﴾ meaning: those whom your eyes despise and belittle, namely the believers, because they said: "They are our lowest." ﴿Allah will not give them any good﴾ meaning: success, faith, or reward. ﴿Allah knows best what is in their souls﴾ of good and evil, more than I do. ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾ if I said this.

﴿They said: "O Nuh, you have disputed with us, and you have multiplied your disputation with us. So bring us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment, ﴿if you are among the truthful."

﴿He said: "Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills﴾ meaning: the punishment, ﴿and you will not escape."﴾ meaning: you will not be able to flee.

﴿And my advice will not benefit you﴾ meaning: my counsel, ﴿if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to lead you astray﴾ meaning: to misguide you. ﴿He is your Lord﴾, to Him belongs the judgment and the command, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah?﴾ Who would protect me from the punishment of Allah.

﴿If I drive them away, will you not then take heed?﴾ Will you not be admonished?

﴿And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾ so that I could bring you whatever you ask for, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾ so that I could tell you what you desire.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 35–37:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: He means Nuh (peace be upon him). Muqatil said: He means Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Say: If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime.﴾ That is: my sin and the burden of my offense. And al-ijram (crime) is the earning of sin.

﴿And I am free from what you commit as crime.﴾ I shall not be held accountable for your sins.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "Indeed, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed."﴾ Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the people of Nuh (peace be upon him) used to beat Nuh until he fell, and they would throw him into a labad [[al-labad: wool; it is said, "He has neither sabad nor labad": he has neither hair nor wool, i.e., he has neither little nor much.]] and throw him into the bottom of a house, thinking that he had died, and he would come out on the second day and call them to Allah, mighty and majestic.

It is related that an elderly man among them came leaning on a staff, with his son with him, and said: "O my son, do not be deceived by this crazy old man." So [the son] said to him: "O father, let me have the staff," and he took the staff from his father and struck Nuh until he gave him a dreadful wound. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed to him [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ishaq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsakir from Ibn ʿAbbas: 4/417, and what Ibn ʿAsakir and the like alone narrate is weak.]] ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾. ﴿So do not be distressed﴾ — that is, do not grieve — ﴿over what they have been doing.﴾ For I will destroy them and deliver you from them. At that point Nuh prayed against them: "He said, 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller.'" [Nuh: 26].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythi that it reached him [[See al-Tabari: 15/313-314, and it is also in al-Tarikh of al-Tabari: 1/92-93.]] that they would seize him and choke him until he fainted; when he regained consciousness he would say: "My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know." This continued until they persisted in disobedience and the trial from them intensified upon him, and he waited for generation after generation, and no generation came except that it was more wicked than the one before it, so much so that the latest of them would say: "This is how it was with our fathers and grandfathers — this madman," and they would accept nothing from him. So he complained to Allah, exalted is He, and said: "My Lord, I have called my people night and day" — until he said: "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed to him:

﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: in Our sight. Muqatil said: with Our knowledge. It was also said: under Our protection.

﴿And by Our revelation﴾ — by Our command.

﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾ By the flood. It was said: its meaning is, do not intercede with Me for the postponement of [[In "b": (destruction).]] the disbelievers, for I have decreed their drowning. It was also said: do not intercede with Me concerning your son Kan'an and your wife Wa'ilah, for both of them are doomed along with the people.

In the narrative [[that al-Tabari related, as mentioned above]] it is said that Jibril came to Nuh (peace be upon him) and said: "Indeed your Lord, mighty and majestic, commands you to construct the ship." He said: "How shall I build it, when I am not a carpenter?" So he said: "Your Lord says: Build, for you are under My eye." So he took the adze and began to work without making a mistake. It was also said: Allah revealed to him that he should make it like the breast of a bird (the prow of a bird) [[In "b": (snout).]].

The Almighty's words: ﴿And he was making the ark﴾. When Allah the Exalted commanded him to make the ark, Nuh (peace be upon him) set about building it and paid no heed to his people. He began cutting the wood, hammering the iron, and preparing the materials for the ark from pitch and other things. His people kept passing by him while he worked, and they mocked him, saying, "O Nuh, have you become a carpenter after being a prophet?" Allah made the wombs of their women barren, so they bore no children. [[From the earlier narrative related from Ibn Ishaq in the report of al-Tabari.]]

The People of the Torah [[Ahl al-Tawrah (the Torah). "Za'ama" (claimed) is a mount of falsehood. We are bound to believe what is in the Noble Book, which falsehood cannot reach from before it or behind it.]] claim that Allah commanded him to make the ark of teak wood, to make it with an azwar [["Azwar" derives from "al-zawr" (with a fatha and then a sukun), meaning the chest, and "al-zawar" (with two fathas), meaning a curvature of the chest, namely that the breastplate of the chest is narrow and the lower chest protrudes, as if it had been squeezed from both sides. See the margin commentary of al-Tabari: 15/314.]], and to coat it with pitch [[Pitch: bitumen. Al-Firuzabadi (al-Qamus) says: a black substance with which camels and ships are coated, or it is bitumen.]] inside and out. He was to make its length eighty cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, the cubit being measured to the shoulder. He was to make it in three decks: lower, middle, and upper, and to make openings in it. Nuh did as Allah the Mighty and Majestic had commanded him.

Ibn Abbas said: Nuh built the ship over two years. Its length was three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits. It was made of teak wood and had three levels. In the lowest level he carried the wild beasts, the predators, and the creeping things; in the middle level, the animals and livestock; and he and those with him rode in the upper level, together with the provisions they needed.

Qatadah said: its door was on its side.

It is also reported from al-Hasan that its length was twelve hundred cubits and its breadth six hundred cubits. But the well-known report is the first: that its length was three hundred cubits.

From Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Nuh (peace be upon him) remained for a hundred years planting trees and cutting them, and for a hundred years building the ark.

It has also been said: he planted the trees for forty years and dried them for forty years.

From Ka'b al-Ahbar: Nuh built the ship in thirty years. It is also reported that it had three tiers: the lowest tier was for the animals and wild beasts, the middle tier was for humans, and the upper tier was for birds. When the dung of the animals accumulated, Allah revealed to Nuh, "Rub the tail of the elephant," and he rubbed it, and a boar and a sow fell out of it, and they set about eating the dung. Then a mouse fell into the hold of the ship and began gnawing at it and at its ropes. Allah revealed to him, "Strike between the eyes of the lion," and he struck it, and a male cat and a female cat came out of its nostril, and they set about the mouse. [[These details about the ship, its length, its tiers, and what was carried in it, and about the creatures and how some were created from others, etc., were also mentioned by al-Tabari and al-Suyuti. They are among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Jewish and Christian origin) that Jews and their like fabricated over the ages. They were widespread and well known in the pre-Islamic period. When Islam came, People of the Scripture who had embraced Islam spread them among the Muslims, and these narrators related them in good faith, without scrutinizing them, relying on the fact that their falsehood is apparent. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) pointed out the strangeness of the report from Ibn Ishaq that was mentioned earlier in al-Baghawi. See Al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahba, pp. 301–305; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/445–446.]]

The Almighty's words: ﴿And whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him.﴾ They used to say, "This man who claims to be a prophet has become a carpenter." It is reported that they would say to him, "O Nuh, what are you doing?" He would reply, "I am building a house that will walk on the water." They would laugh at him. ﴿He said: If you mock us, then we mock you﴾ when you witness the punishment of Allah, ﴿just as you mock.﴾ If it is asked, "How is it permissible to mock a prophet?" It is said: this is a figure of speech of mutual correspondence; it means, "If you treat me with ignorance, then I shall treat you with ignorance when the punishment descends upon you." It has also been said: its meaning is, "If you mock us, then you will see the outcome of your mockery."

﴿So you will surely know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him﴾ — that will humiliate him. ﴿And upon whom will descend﴾ — that will be obligatory for him, ﴿a lasting punishment﴾ — enduring.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 40:

﴿Until, when Our command came﴾, meaning Our punishment, ﴿and the oven gushed forth﴾. The scholars differed concerning the "oven" (al-tannur) [[See on this: al-Tabari: 15/318-321.]]. ʿIkrimah and al-Zuhri said: it is the surface of the earth, because it was said to Noah: "When you see the water gushing forth over the surface of the earth, board the ship."

It is narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The oven gushed forth" means: the dawn rose and the light of morning appeared.

al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi said: it is the oven in which bread is baked, and this is the view of most of the exegetes [[al-Tabari favoured this view, saying: "The most preferable of the sayings regarding the meaning of His words 'al-tannur' in our view is the saying of the one who said: 'It is the oven in which bread is baked,' because that is the well-known usage in the speech of the Arabs. The speech of Allah is not directed except to the most prevalent and most famous of its meanings among the Arabs, unless there is a proof concerning something of it to the contrary, which is then to be accepted. For He, may His praise be exalted, addressed them with what He addressed them with in order to make them understand the meaning of what He addressed them with." al-Tabari: 15/321.]].

And the narration of ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas: al-Hasan said: it was an oven of stone, which Eve used to bake in. It passed to Noah, peace be upon him, and it was said to Noah: "When you see the water boiling out of the oven, board, you and your companions."

They differed concerning its location [[See: al-Tabari: 15/320-321.]]. Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi said: it was in the district of Kufa, [and al-Shaʿbi used to swear: "The oven only gushed forth from the district of Kufa"] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]]. He said: Noah built the ship inside the mosque of Kufa, and the oven was on the right of the one entering from the side of the Kindah Gate, and the gushing of the water from it was a sign for Noah, peace be upon him.

Muqatil said: that was the oven of Adam, and it was in Syria, in a place called ʿAyn Wardah.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it was in India.

And al-fawaran means: boiling.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿We said: carry in it﴾, meaning in the ship, ﴿of every kind two of each pair﴾. The "zawjan" (pair) is every two that cannot do without one another; each of the two is called a zawj (mate). It is said: a zawj of a shoe and a zawj of a sandal. And what is meant by the two pairs here is: the male and the female.

Hafs recited here, and in Surat al-Mu'minun, "min kullin" with tanwin, meaning: "of every kind two pairs," mentioning it for emphasis.

In the story: Noah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "My Lord, how can I carry of every kind two of each pair?" So Allah gathered to him the beasts and the birds, and he began striking with his hand at each kind, so the male fell into his right hand and the female into his left hand, and he carried them in the ship.

﴿And your family﴾, meaning: carry your family, that is, your children and dependants, ﴿except for him against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ of destruction, meaning: his wife Wa'ilah and his son Kan'an, ﴿and those who believe﴾, meaning: carry those who believe in you, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾. And they differed concerning their number [[See these sayings: al-Tabari: 15/325-327. He said: "The correct statement on this matter is to say as Allah said: 'And none believed with him except a few,' describing them as being few, and He did not set their number by a specific quantity, nor is there a sound report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So one should not exceed the limit set by Allah in this matter, when there is no limit to the number of them in the Book of Allah or in a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."]]: Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi said: there were only eight persons in the ship: Noah, his wife, and his three sons Sam, Ham and Yafith, and their wives. [[Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "It is also said: Noah's wife was with them in the ship. But this is open to question; rather, the apparent view is that she perished, because she was upon the religion of her people, so what befell them befell her, just as what befell the wife of Lot befell her people. And Allah knows best and is most wise." al-Tafsir: 2/446.]]

al-Aʿmash said: they were seven: Noah and his three sons, and his three daughters-in-law.

Ibn Ishaq said: they were ten besides their wives: Noah and his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith, and six men of those who had believed in him, and their wives all together.

Muqatil said: they were seventy-two persons: a man and a woman, his three sons and their wives; all together they were seventy-eight, half of them men and half of them women.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: there were eighty men in Noah's ship, one of them being Jurhum.

Muqatil said: Noah carried with him the body of Adam, and placed it crosswise between the men and the women. And all the beasts and birds approached Noah so that he would carry them.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: the first thing Noah carried was the ant, and the last thing he carried was the donkey. When the donkey entered and its chest went in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its two legs could not move. Noah kept saying: "Woe to you, enter!" but it rose and could not. Until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter, even though the devil is with you" — a word slipped from his tongue. When Noah said it, the devil released its path, so it entered, and the devil entered too. Noah said to him: "What brought you in upon me, O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Did you not say: 'Enter, even though the devil is with you'?" He said: "Get out from me, O enemy of Allah." He said: "You have no choice but to carry me with you." So he was, as they claim, on the back of the ark.

It is narrated from some of them that the snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: "Carry us." He said: "You are the cause of harm and affliction, so I will not carry you." They said to him: "Carry us, and we guarantee you that we will not harm anyone who mentions you. So whoever, when he fears their harm, recites 'Peace be upon Noah among the worlds,' they will not harm him."

al-Hasan said: Noah did not carry in the ship except what gives birth or lays eggs. As for what is generated from the mud among the insects of the earth, such as bedbugs and mosquitoes, he carried none of them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 41–43:

Muhammad ibn Muhaysin read "مَجْرِيهَا وَمَرْسَاهَا" with a fatha on both mims, from جَرَتْ and رَسَتْ, meaning [In the name of Allah] its running (jaryuha) and its anchoring (rusuwwuha), and both are verbal nouns (masdar). The others read "مُجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا" with a damma on both mims, from أُجْرِيَتْ and أُرْسِيَتْ, meaning: In the name of Allah is its causing to run (ijra'uha) and its causing to anchor (irsa'uha) [and both of these are also verbal nouns] [[Omitted from "A". For these readings and their justification see al-Tabari, 15/327–330.]], like His saying: "أَنْزِلْنِي مُنْزَلًا مُبَارَكًا" [al-Mu'minun: 29] and "أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ" [al-Isra': 80]. What is meant by them is causing to descend, entering and exiting.

﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ Al-Dahhak said: Whenever Nuh wanted the ship to run, he would say, "In the name of Allah," and it would run; and whenever he wanted it to anchor, he would say, "In the name of Allah," and it would anchor.

﴿وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ فِي مَوْجٍ كَالْجِبَالِ﴾ The wave (mawj) is what rises from the water when the wind blows hard upon it. He compared it to mountains in its size and its height above the water.

﴿وَنَادَى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ﴾ Kan'an. Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Sam. He was a disbeliever. ﴿وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ﴾ apart from him; he had not boarded the ship. ﴿يَا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنَا﴾ [Ibn Amir, Hamzah, Asim and Ya'qub read it with the ba' clearly pronounced (izhar), while the others assimilate it into the mim (idgham)], ﴿وَلَا تَكُنْ مَعَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ so that you perish.

﴿قَالَ﴾ His son said: ﴿سَآوِي﴾ "I will go up and take refuge," ﴿إِلَى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الْمَاءِ﴾ "to a mountain that will protect me from the water," i.e., prevent me from drowning. ﴿قَالَ﴾ Nuh said to him: ﴿لَا عَاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ "There is no protector today from the command of Allah," i.e., from the punishment of Allah, ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ﴾ "except for the one on whom He has mercy." It is said: "مَنْ" is in the nominative position, meaning: there is no preventer from the punishment of Allah except Allah, the Merciful. And it is said: "مَنْ" is in the accusative position, meaning: there is no one protected except the one whom Allah has shown mercy to, like His saying: "فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ" [al-Haqqah: 21], meaning "مَرْضِيَّةٍ" (pleasing). ﴿وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا الْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ﴾ So the wave came between them, and he became ﴿مِنَ الْمُغْرَقِينَ﴾ among the drowned.

It is related that the water rose over the mountaintops by about forty cubits. [It is also said: fifteen cubits] [[Omitted from "B".]].

It is related that when the water increased in the streets, a mother of a child, who loved him very intensely, feared for him. She went up the mountain until she reached its third, and when the water reached her she climbed until she reached its two-thirds. When it reached her she went on until she stood at the top of the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she raised the child with her hands until the water carried them both away. Had Allah had mercy on any of them, He would have had mercy on the child's mother. [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2/342, who authenticated it, and al-Dhahabi said: its chain is dark (muzlim), and Musa is not reliable. It has been mentioned in this story that Allah dried up the loins of the fathers and rendered the wombs of the women barren forty years before the punishment, and it is said seventy years; and there were no children among them at the time of the punishment, based on His saying: "وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ" [al-Furqan/al-Qamar-type verse as cited], so the disbelief of children did not occur; therefore the account of the child's mother is wondrous. It may be said that it is permissible that their age of maturity was beyond seventy because of their long lives, so there were children among them and the punishment encompassed them. It may also be said that there are two reports on this: the first is that Allah dried up the loins of their fathers and rendered the wombs of their women barren forty or seventy years before the punishment, and there were no children at the time of the punishment. In another report that drying and barrenness did not occur, so children existed among them at the time of the punishment, following their disbelieving fathers in the punishment of this world. As for the punishment of the Hereafter, there are two opinions. Some say they are in the Hereafter with their disbelieving fathers, and others say they are in Paradise, which is the more sound and stronger view. End of the quotation, abridged, from the margin of "A" with some editing.]].

﴿And it was said﴾, meaning, after the matter of the Flood had come to an end: ﴿O earth, swallow up your water﴾, drink it in, ﴿and O sky, withhold﴾, hold back. ﴿The water subsided﴾, decreased and dried up. It is said: *ghāḍa al-māʾu yaghīḍu ghayḍan* (the water receded, decreasing), and *ghāḍahu Allāh* means God reduced it. ﴿And the matter was decided﴾, meaning the affair was completed, which is the destruction of the people. ﴿And it came to rest﴾, meaning the ship settled ﴿on al-Jūdī﴾, a mountain in al-Jazīrah (Upper Mesopotamia) near Mosul. ﴿And it was said: "Away with﴾, meaning destruction ﴿the wrongdoing people!"﴾.

It is related that Noah, peace be upon him, sent the raven to bring him news of the earth, but it alighted upon a carcass and did not return. So he sent the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and its feet smeared with mud, and Noah knew that the water had dried up. It is said that he invoked fear upon the raven, which is why it does not become familiar with houses. He placed the green collar around the dove's neck and prayed for it security, which is why it is safe and becomes familiar with houses. [[See what has passed, p. (177), a note. [[al-Sājī said: al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, al-Shāfiʿī narrated to us, he said: It was said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd: Did your father narrate to you from your grandfather that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, the ship of Noah circumambulated the House seven times and prayed two rakʿas behind the Station"? He said: Yes. Al-Sājī said: He is munkar al-ḥadīth (a narrator of rejected reports). Al-Ṭaḥāwī said: His narration, according to the people of hadith scholarship, is extremely weak. Al-Ḥākim and Abū Nuʿaym said: He narrated from his father fabricated reports. See: al-Tahdhīb 6/162, and the previous note.]]].

It is related that Noah, peace be upon him, boarded the ship on the tenth of Rajab, and the ship sailed with them for six months. It passed by the House (the Kaʿbah) and circumambulated it seven times (4), and God had raised it from the drowning while its site remained. They descended on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, so Noah fasted, and he commanded everyone with him to fast in thanksgiving to God, Mighty and Majestic.

It is also said: none of the disbelievers escaped the drowning except ʿŪj ibn ʿUnuq, for the water reached only to his waist. The cause of his salvation was that Noah needed teak wood for the ship, but he could not carry it, so ʿŪj brought it to him from Syria, and God, exalted be He, saved him from drowning because of that. [[The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, mentioned the report of ʿŪj ibn ʿUnuq as an example of what the sound evidences have established to be false: "... It is not strange that such a liar should be bold against God; what is strange is that someone includes this report in books of knowledge, such as tafsir and others, without clarifying its status. They consider him a descendant of Noah, yet God, exalted be He, said: ﴿And We made his descendants the ones who remain﴾ (al-Ṣāffāt 37:77). He informed us that everyone who remains upon the face of the earth is of Noah's descendants. So if ʿŪj had existed, he would not have remained after Noah." al-Manār al-Munīf fī al-Ṣaḥīḥ wa al-Ḍaʿīf, p. (77). **Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 11, verses 45–46:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family,"﴾ and You had promised me that You would save me and my family? ﴿And indeed Your promise is the truth﴾ with no breaking of it, ﴿and You are the most just of judges﴾ who judges that some people are to be saved and others destroyed.

﴿He said﴾ Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿"O Noah, indeed he is not of your family. Indeed, he is [one whose] deed is unrighteous."﴾ Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read ﴿عَمِلَ﴾ ('amila, with a kasra on the mim and a fatha on the lam) and ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ (ghayra, with a fatha on the ra' as a verb-object), meaning: he committed polytheism and denial. The others read ﴿عَمَلٌ﴾ ('amalun, with a fatha on the mim and a damma on the lam, with tanwin), and ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ (ghayru, with a damma on the ra'), meaning: your request to me to save him is an unrighteous deed. ﴿So do not ask Me﴾ O Noah, ﴿about that of which you have no knowledge.﴾

"They said, 'O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof (bayyinah), and we are not going to abandon our gods because of your word, nor are we going to believe you.'"

"We only say that some of our gods have struck you with some evil," meaning: that some of our gods have afflicted you with harm. "You are not engaging in opposing us and reviling our gods except that some of our gods have struck you, that is, afflicted you with harm, with madness and insanity. That is because you reviled our gods, so they have taken revenge on you by deranging you. We interpret your matter only in this way." Hud said to them, "I call God to witness against myself, and you bear witness, O my people, that I am free of what you associate" (with Him).

"Other than Him," meaning: the idols. "So scheme against me, all of you together, then devise your plots and harm me, you and your idols, and give me no respite (la tunzirun)," meaning: do not delay and do not give me time.

"Indeed I have put my trust in God (tawakkaltu), that is, I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature (dabbah) but that He holds its forelock (nasiyah)." Al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and causes it to die.

Al-Farra' said: its Owner and the One who has power over it.

Al-Qutaybi said: He subdues it, for whoever you have seized by the forelock, you have subdued.

It is also said: the forelock was singled out for mention because the Arabs use this expression when they describe a person as humbled. They say, "The forelock of so-and-so is in the hand of so-and-so." When they captured a person and wished to release him and show him favor, they would cut his forelock so that they might boast of this over him. So God addressed them in terms they understood.

"Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path," meaning: although my Lord is able to overpower them, He does not wrong them and does not act except with goodness and justice, rewarding the one who does good for his goodness and the one who does evil for his disobedience. It is also said: the meaning is that the religion of my Lord is upon a straight path.

It is also said that there is an implied element in it: that is, my Lord urges you and guides you onto a straight path.

"Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path," meaning: although my Lord is able to overpower them, He does not wrong them and does not act except with goodness and justice, rewarding the one who does good for his goodness and the one who does evil for his disobedience. It is also said: the meaning is that the religion of my Lord is upon a straight path.

It is also said that there is an implied element in it: that is, my Lord urges you and guides you onto a straight path.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 57–60:**

﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., "you turn away" (*tatawallaw*), meaning: you turn away from that to which I have called you. ﴿Then I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with to you, and my Lord will replace you with another people﴾, i.e., if you turn away, God, mighty and majestic, will destroy you and replace you with a people other than you, more obedient than you, who will affirm His oneness and worship Him. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾ by your turning away and your aversion; you only harm yourselves. It is also said: you will not diminish Him at all if He destroys you, because your existence and your non-existence are equal to Him. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, i.e., a Guardian over everything, who protects me from your reaching me with harm.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came﴾, meaning Our punishment, ﴿We saved Hud and those who believed with him﴾, and they were four thousand.

﴿By mercy﴾, i.e., by a blessing ﴿from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment﴾, which was the wind with which He destroyed ʿAd. It is also said: the harsh punishment is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, i.e., just as We saved them from punishment in this world, so We saved them in the Hereafter.

﴿And that was ʿAd﴾, he referred to them as the tribe, ﴿who denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers﴾, meaning Hud alone. He mentioned it in the plural form because whoever denies one messenger is like one who denies all the messengers. ﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾, i.e., the base and the lowly followed the people of arrogance and stubbornness. The *jabbar* (tyrant) is the arrogant one, and the *ʿanid* (obstinate) is the one who does not accept the truth. It is said: "ʿanida al-rajul yaʿnidu ʿunudan" when a man refuses to accept a thing even though he knows it. Abu ʿUbayda said: *al-ʿanid*, *al-ʿanid*, *al-ʿanud*, and *al-muʿanid* all mean one who opposes you with contradiction.

﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾, i.e., a curse was sent after them, which overtook them and went with them. *Al-laʿna* (curse) is distance and expulsion from mercy. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection as well they will be cursed, just as they were cursed in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Unquestionably, ʿAd disbelieved in their Lord﴾, i.e., "in their Lord" [it is said: *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, just as it is said: *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*, and *nasahtuhu* and *nasahtu lahu*].

﴿Unquestionably, away with ʿAd, the people of Hud﴾. It is said: "away" means far from the mercy of God. It is also said: destruction. *Al-buʿd* (distance) has two meanings: one is the opposite of nearness, from which it is said: *baʿuda yabʿudu buʿdan*; the other means destruction, from which it is said: *baʿida yabʿadu baʿdan wa buʿdan*.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 61–62:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾, meaning: We sent to Thamud their brother Salih in lineage [not in religion]. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah﴾, i.e., make Allah, mighty and majestic, One [wahhidu Allah; in one manuscript: "wahhaduhu"]. ﴿You have no god other than Him. He produced you from the earth﴾, i.e., began your creation, ﴿from the earth﴾. That is because they descended from Adam, peace be upon him, and Adam was created from the earth. ﴿And He made you inhabit it﴾, i.e., made you its cultivators (u mmar) and its settlers (sukkan). Al-Dahhak said: He lengthened your lifespans in it, until one of them would live three hundred years up to a thousand years. And likewise the people of ʿAd.

Mujahid said: "a'malakum" is from al-'umra, meaning He made it yours for as long as you live. Qatadah said: He settled you in it.

﴿So seek His forgiveness, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Near﴾ to the believers, ﴿Responsive﴾ to their supplication.

﴿They said﴾, meaning Thamud: ﴿O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this﴾ saying. [I.e., we used to hope] that you would become a leader among us. It was also said: we used to hope that you would return to our religion, for they were hoping for his return to the religion of his tribe. When he openly called them to Allah, mighty and majestic, and abandoned the idols, they thought their hope in him had been cut off, and so they said: ﴿Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped﴾ of the gods [before this]? ﴿And indeed we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us﴾, one that causes suspicion and accusation. It is said: "arabtuhu irabatan" when you do to him an act that makes him suspicious.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 63–65:

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself,"﴾ meaning prophethood and wisdom, ﴿"then who will help me against God? That is, who will prevent me from God's [punishment]? [Omitted in manuscript B.] If I disobey Him, you would only increase me in loss."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: its meaning is: you would add nothing but loss to your own loss.

Al-Husayn [In B: "al-Hasan"] ibn al-Fadl said: Salih (peace be upon him) was not in loss, so that he could say "you would only increase me in loss." Rather, the meaning is: by what you say, you increase me only in attributing you to loss.

In the language, *al-tafsiq* (attributing someone to wickedness) and *al-tafjir* (attributing someone to depravity) mean attributing a person to *fisq* (sin) and *fujur* (immorality), and likewise *al-takhsir* (attributing someone to loss) means attributing a person to *khusran* (loss).

﴿"And O my people, this is God's she-camel, a sign for you."﴾ The word *hadhihi* (this) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*hal*) and as a detached qualifier (*qat'*). The reason is that his people asked him to bring forth a pregnant she-camel from this rock, and they pointed to a rock. Salih (peace be upon him) prayed, and a she-camel came out of it and immediately gave birth to a young one like herself. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿"So leave her to eat on God's earth,"﴾ from the herbage and plants, ﴿"and do not touch her with harm,"﴾ and do not strike her to hamstring her, ﴿"or a near punishment will seize you."﴾ [Its upkeep is not your responsibility.] If you kill her, a near punishment will seize you.

﴿Then they hamstrung her, and he said,﴾ Salih said: ﴿"Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days."﴾ That is, live in your dwellings. ﴿"Then you will be destroyed. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ That is, not a lie.

It is reported that he told them: "The punishment will come to you after three days. On the first day your faces will be yellow, on the second day red, and on the third day black." It happened as he said, and the punishment came to them on the fourth day.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 11, verses 66–69**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾, meaning by a blessing from Us. ﴿And from the disgrace of that Day﴾, meaning from His punishment and humiliation.

Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and al-Kisa'i recited *khizyi yawma'idhin* (خِزْيِ يَوْمَئِذٍ) and *adhabi yawma'idhin* (عَذَابِ يَوْمَئِذٍ) with a fatha on the *mim* (فَتْحِ الْمِيمِ). The rest recited them with a kasra (بِالْكَسْرِ).

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty﴾.

﴿And those who wronged﴾, meaning disbelieved, ﴿were seized by the blast﴾. This was because Jibril, upon him be peace, cried out at them with a single cry, and they all perished. It was also said: there came upon them a cry from the sky containing the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything on earth, so their hearts burst within their breasts. He said *wa akhadha* ("and seized") although *al-sayhah* ("the blast") is feminine, because *al-sayhah* carries the meaning of *al-siyah* (the outcry).

﴿So they became, in their homes, prostrate﴾, meaning fallen and dead.

﴿As if they had never flourished therein﴾, meaning had never dwelt and lived there. ﴿Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ Hamzah, Hafs and Ya'qub recited *Thamuda* (ثَمُودَ) without tanwin (nunation), and likewise in Surat al-Furqan, al-Ankabut and al-Najm. Abu Bakr agreed with them concerning al-Najm. The rest recited it with tanwin. Al-Kisa'i recited *li-Thamudin* (لِثَمُودٍ) with a kasra on the *dal* and with tanwin, while the rest recited it with a fatha on the *dal*. Whoever recited it with a kasra did so because it is a masculine proper noun, and whoever did not put it in the genitive treated it as the name of a tribe.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good tidings﴾. By "messengers" He means the angels. The scholars differed concerning their number [[See these opinions in: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/241.]]. Ibn Abbas and Ata' said: they were three: Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil.

Al-Dahhak said: they were nine.

Muqatil said: they were twelve angels.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Jibril was there, and with him were seven.

Al-Suddi said: they were eleven angels in the form of handsome youths with radiant faces.

﴿With the good tidings﴾, meaning the glad tidings of Ishaq and Ya'qub. It was also said: the glad tidings of the destruction of the people of Lut.

﴿They said, "Peace."﴾ That is, they greeted him with peace. ﴿He said, "Peace"﴾, meaning: peace be upon you. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 70–71:

﴿When he saw that their hands did not reach toward it﴾, meaning toward the calf, ﴿he regarded them with suspicion﴾, meaning he disapproved of them, ﴿and felt a fear within himself﴾, meaning he concealed fear. Muqatil said: it fell into his heart. The root of wujus is "entering": the fear had entered his heart. Qatadah said: this was because when a guest came to them and did not eat their food, they thought he had not come with good, but with evil.

﴿They said: Fear not﴾, O Ibrahim, [﴿we are messengers of your Lord.﴾ That is:] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] ﴿We have been sent﴾ as angels of God ﴿to the people of Lut﴾.

﴿And his wife﴾ was Sarah, daughter of Haran ibn Ahwar [[In manuscript "B": (taken from).]], and she was the daughter of Ibrahim's paternal uncle.

﴿Standing﴾ behind the screen, listening to their speech. It was also said: she was standing serving the messengers, while Ibrahim was sitting with them.

﴿Then she laughed﴾. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: she laughed, meaning she menstruated at that moment. The Arabs say: "the female hare laughed," meaning she menstruated. Most scholars hold that the intended meaning is the well-known laughter.

They differed about the reason for her laughter. It was said: she laughed because the fear had left her and Ibrahim when they said, "Fear not." Al-Suddi said: when Ibrahim brought the food near them and they did not eat, Ibrahim feared and thought them thieves, so he said to them, "Will you not eat?" They said, "We do not eat food except for a price." Ibrahim said, "Then it has a price." They said, "And what is its price?" He said, "You mention God's name over its beginning and praise Him at its end." Jibril looked at Mika'il and said, "He is worthy that his Lord should take him as a close friend (khalil)." When Ibrahim and Sarah saw that their hands did not reach toward it, Sarah laughed and said, "How strange! Our guests: we serve them ourselves out of honour for them, and yet they do not eat our food."

Qatadah said: she laughed at the heedlessness of the people of Lut and the nearness of punishment to them.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: she laughed at Ibrahim's fear of the three [[Omitted from manuscript "B"]] [in his house], while he was among his servants and retinue.

It was also said: she laughed out of joy at the good news.

Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: she laughed in amazement that she should have a child despite her old age and her husband's old age.

According to this view, the verse is in inverted order (taqdim wa ta'khir), its sense being: "His wife was standing, so We gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub. She laughed and said, 'Woe is me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman?'"

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq﴾, meaning after Ishaq, ﴿Ya'qub﴾, by which is meant the father of the child. She was given the good news that she would live until she saw the child of her child. Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and Hafs read Ya'qub with a fatha on the ba' (nasb), meaning: and after Ishaq We gave Ya'qub. It was also said: by supposing a verb, meaning: and We bestowed upon him [after] Ya'qub. [[Omitted from manuscript "B".]] The rest read it in the nominative (raf'), by omitting the preposition of the attribute. It was also said: "and after Ishaq, Ya'qub will be born." When she was given the good news of a child, she laughed, then she struck her face, meaning she slapped her face in amazement.

﴿So when the fear had left Abraham, and the good news had come to him, concerning Isaac and Jacob, he began to dispute with Us concerning the people of Lot.﴾ The "fear" (al-ruʿw) is dread. There is an implied element here: the meaning is "he began and kept on disputing with Us."

It is said: the meaning is that he spoke with Us, because Abraham, peace be upon him, would not dispute with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic; he would only ask Him and make entreaty to Him.

The majority of the scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) said: the meaning is that he disputed with Our messengers. His dispute was that he said to the angels: "Tell me, if there were fifty believers in the cities of Lot, would you destroy them?" They said: "No." He said: "Or forty?" They said: "No." He said: "Or thirty?" They said: "No," until he reached five. [They said: "No."] [[Omitted from "b".]] He said: "Tell me, if there were in them one Muslim man, would you destroy them?" They said: "No." Then Abraham, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, Lot is in it." They said: "We know best who is in it. We will save him and his family, except for his wife; she was among those who remained behind."

﴿Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and turning back in repentance.﴾ Ibn Jurayj said: In the villages of the people of Lot there were four thousand thousand (four million) [people]. Then the messengers said to Abraham at that point:

﴿O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed a punishment that cannot be turned back is coming upon them.﴾ That is: turn away from this speech and leave off the argument. "The command of your Lord has come" means: the punishment of your Lord [and the decree of your Lord] [[Omitted from "b".]]. "A punishment that cannot be turned back" means: one that will not be averted from them.

The Most High's saying: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾ means these angels, ﴿in the form of beardless young men of handsome faces;﴾ ﴿he was distressed by them﴾ means Lot was grieved by their coming. It is said: "I made him sad (suʾtuhu), so he became sad (sīʾa)," just as it is said: "I made him happy (sarartuhu), so he became happy (surra)."

﴿And he felt helpless for them﴾ means his heart was constricted. It is said: "The chest (dharʿ) of so-and-so became constricted over such-and-such" when he falls into something disliked from which he cannot bear to get out. This was because when Lot, peace be upon him, saw the beauty of their faces and the pleasantness of their scent, he feared for them from his people, that they would intend them for the foul deed, and he knew he would need to defend them.

﴿And he said, "This is a distressing day."﴾ That is: severe, as if evil and calamity were bound to it (ʿuṣiba), that is, tightened.

Qatada and al-Suddi said: The angels left Abraham, peace be upon him, toward the town of Lot, and they came to Lot at midday, while he was in a piece of land of his, working in it.

It is also said: he was gathering firewood. Almighty God had said to them: "Do not destroy them until Lot testifies against them four times." So they asked him to host them, and he set off with them. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 78:

﴿And his people came hastening towards him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas [and Qatadah] said: they were hurrying towards him. Mujahid said: they were running (yuhaarwiluun). Al-Hasan said: a walk between two gaits. Shimr ibn 'Atiyyah said: between running (al-harwalah) [and jamz (a quick trot)] [in B: al-khabb (a fast trot)].

﴿And before this﴾, that is, before their coming to Lot, ﴿they used to do evil deeds﴾, meaning they used to have intercourse with men in their posteriors.

﴿He said﴾ to them, when they set out for his guests and thought they were young men, Lot said: ﴿O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you﴾. He meant: in marriage. And in [the Arabic text reads "wa-fi", likely "wa-qad", i.e. the text is uncertain] his guests with his daughters. At that time, marrying a Muslim woman to a disbeliever was permissible, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) married his daughter to 'Utbah ibn Abi Lahab and Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi' before the revelation, and both of them were disbelievers [narrated by Ibn Hisham, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il; see al-Kafi al-Shaf, pp. 86-87].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: he offered his daughters to them on condition of Islam.

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: his saying ﴿these are my daughters﴾ meant: their women, and he attributed them to himself because every prophet is a father to his community. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers" [al-Ahzab 33:6], and he is a father to them.

It was said: he mentioned this by way of deflection, not as a definite proposal, and they did not accept this.

﴿So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests﴾ [i.e. fear God and do not shame me concerning my guests], that is: do not offend me and do not expose me regarding my guests.

﴿Is there not among you a man of sound judgement?﴾ — upright and rightly guided. 'Ikrimah said: a man who says, "There is no god but Allah." Ibn Ishaq said: a man who enjoins good and forbids evil.

﴿They said: "You certainly know,"﴾ O Lut, ﴿"that we have no right to your daughters."﴾ That is, they are not our wives, so we would have no right to them through marriage. It was also said that the meaning is: "We have no need or desire for them."

﴿"And you certainly know what we want,"﴾ namely, having intercourse with men.

﴿He said﴾ to them, at that point, Lut: ﴿"If only I had power against you,"﴾ he meant physical strength, or strength through followers, ﴿"or could take refuge in a strong support."﴾ That is, that I could join a protecting clan. The response to "law" (if only) is omitted, meaning: "We would have fought you and come between you and them."

Abu Hurayrah said: "Allah did not send any prophet after him except one who had protection from his clan."

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] informed us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed us: Abu al-Zinad informed us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Lut; he used to take refuge in a strong support." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Stories of the Prophets, chapter "And Lut, when he said to his people: Do you commit an abomination while you see?": 6/415.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas and the exegetes said: Lut locked his door while the angels were with him in the house. He was arguing with them and pleading with them from behind the door, while they were trying to climb over the wall. When the angels saw what Lut was suffering because of them, they said:

﴿"O Lut,"﴾ indeed your support is strong. ﴿"We are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you."﴾ So open the door and leave us and them. He opened the door and they entered. Then Gabriel asked his Lord, mighty and majestic, for permission to punish them, and He permitted him. He stood in the form in which he appears, spread his wing, and he had a sash of strung pearls on him. He had shining front teeth and a bright forehead, and his hair was curled like coral, and he was as white as snow, while his feet were tending toward green. He struck their faces with his wing, blinded their eyes and made them blind, so they could no longer find the way or reach their houses. They turned back saying: "Flee, flee! In the house of Lut there are the most skilled sorcerers on earth, who have bewitched us!" They kept saying: "O Lut, stay as you are until morning, and you will see what we will do to you tomorrow." They threatened him. Lut said to the angels: "When is the appointed time for their destruction?" They said: "The morning." He said: "I want it sooner than that; if only you would destroy them now." They said: ﴿"Is not the morning near?"﴾ Then they said: ﴿"So travel,"﴾ O Lut, ﴿"with your family"﴾.
