﴿"At a part of the night."﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "At a portion of the night." Al-Dahhak said: "At a remaining part." Qatadah said: "After the first part has passed." It was also said: it refers to the first last third of the night.

﴿"And let none of you look back, except your wife."﴾ Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read "imra'atuka" with a raised ta' (as a nominative), as an exception from "lookingback": meaning, none of you shall look back except your wife, for she will look back and perish. Lut had brought her out with him, and he forbade those who followed him, from among those who travelled with them, to look back, except his wife. When she heard the crash of the punishment, she looked back and said: "O my people!" Then a stone overtook her and killed her.

The others read it with a fatha on the ta' (accusative), as an exception from the travelling (al-israʾ): meaning, "travel with your family, except your wife; do not travel with her, and leave her with her people, for her inclination is toward them." Its confirmation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "So travel with your family at a part of the night, except your wife, and let none of you look back."

﴿"Indeed, what befalls them will befall her."﴾ That is, the punishment. ﴿"Indeed, their appointed time is the morning."﴾ That is, the time of their destruction is the morning. Lut said: "I want it sooner than that." They said: ﴿"Is not the morning near?"﴾

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil** (Baghawi)

**"Then when Our command came"**, meaning Our punishment, **"We made its uppermost part its nethermost"**. Jibril (peace be upon him) inserted his wing beneath the towns of the people of Lut, the overturned cities (al-Mu'tafikat). They were five cities, containing four hundred thousand people. It is also said that there were four thousand thousand. He lifted all the cities until the people of the heavens heard the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs. No vessel was overturned for them, and no sleeper awoke. Then he turned them over and made their uppermost part their nethermost.

**"And We rained down upon it"**, that is, upon its stragglers and travelers. It is also said that after He overturned it, He rained down upon it **"stones of sijjil"**. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: (sang u gil), which is a Persian word that has been Arabicized (mu'arrab).

Qatadah and Ikrimah said: *al-sijjil* is clay. Its evidence is the statement of the Mighty and Majestic: **"to send down upon them stones of clay"** [al-Dhariyat: 33].

Mujahid said: [[In (B): Ibn 'Abbas said.]] its first part is stone and its last part is clay.

Al-Hasan said: the origin of the stones was clay, and then it was hardened.

Al-Dahhak said: it means baked brick (al-ajurr).

It is also said: *al-sijjil* is the name of the lowest heaven. [[Said by Abu al-'Aliyah and Ibn Zayd. This is weak, because it is described as "piled up" (mandud). See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/249.]]

It is also said: it is mountains in the sky. Allah the Exalted said: **"And He sends down from the sky mountains containing hail"** [al-Nur: 43].

The statement of the Exalted: **"piled up" (mandud)**. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: consecutive, one following another. It is a passive participle from *al-nadd*, which means placing one thing upon another.

**"Marked" (musawwamah)** describes the stones, and it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). Its meaning is marked (mu'allamah). Ibn Jurayj said: they had distinguishing marks that did not resemble the stones of the earth.

Qatadah and Ikrimah said: they had red streaks in the form of carnelian (al-ja'z).

Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: they were sealed, with marks like seal rings.

It is also said: on every stone was written the name of the one it was thrown at.

**"With your Lord. And it is not"**, meaning those stones, **"far from the wrongdoers"**, that is, the polytheists of Makkah. Qatadah and Ikrimah said: it means the wrongdoers of this Ummah. By Allah, Allah has never spared any wrongdoer from it since.

In some reports: "There is no wrongdoer except that he is at the edge of a stone that will fall upon him from hour to hour."

It is also reported that the stone followed their stragglers and travelers wherever they were in the lands. A man among them entered the Haram, and the stone remained suspended in the sky for forty days until he came out, and it struck him and destroyed him.

The statement of the Mighty and Majestic: **"And to Madyan"**, meaning: We sent to the descendants of Madyan **"their brother Shu'ayb. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale"**, that is, do not cheat them. They used to give short measure despite their polytheism. **"Indeed, I see you in prosperity."** Ibn 'Abbas said: affluent in blessings. Mujahid said: in abundance and plenty. So he warned them of the loss of blessings, the rise of prices, and the descent of punishment if they did not repent. He said: **"And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing day"**, which will surround you and destroy you.

﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight﴾, complete them, ﴿with justice﴾, with fairness. It was also said: with straightening the tongue of the balance. ﴿And do not deprive people of their due﴾, do not diminish them, ﴿and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾.

﴿What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: it means that what Allah leaves for you of lawful gain after giving full measure and weight is better than what you take through fraud (tatfif). Mujahid said: "Baqiyyat Allah" means the obedience of Allah. ﴿Is better for you, if you are believers﴾, in that what you have of the provision and bounty of Allah is better.

﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾, a custodian. It was said: he said this because he had not been commanded to fight them.

﴿They said: O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped﴾, of the idols. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, prayed a great deal, and that is why they said this. Al-A'mash said: it means: is your recitation (of the Qur'an)?

﴿Or that we should not do with our wealth what we wish﴾, of increasing and decreasing.

It was also said: Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had forbidden them to clip dinars and dirhams, and he claimed that it was unlawful for them. So they said: "Or that we should not do with our wealth what we wish", of clipping them. [[See: al-Tabari: 15/450-451.]]

﴿Indeed you are the forbearing, the discerning﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they meant: the foolish, the misguided. The Arabs describe a thing by its opposite, saying of the one bitten by a snake "the safe one" (salim), and of the desert wasteland "the place of safety" (mafazah). [And it was said] [[In "B": (wa-qad), which is more fitting to the context.]] they said this in mockery.

It was also said: its meaning is "the forbearing, the discerning" according to your claim.

It was also said: it is meant literally, that is, "You, O Shu'ayb, are among us forbearing and discerning; it does not befit you to split the unity of your people or oppose their religion", just as the people of Salih, peace be upon him, said: ﴿You were among us a man in whom we placed our hopes before this﴾ [Hud: 62].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 88–90:

﴿He said: "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has provided me with good provision from Him,"﴾ clear insight and proof. "Good provision" means lawful. It was also said: abundant. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was rich in wealth. It was also said: "good provision" means knowledge and understanding.

﴿"And I do not intend to oppose you in what I forbid you from"﴾, meaning: I do not intend to forbid you from something and then commit it myself.

﴿"I intend only reform, as far as I am able. And my success is not except through Allah."﴾ "Tawfiq" (divine success) means facilitating the path of goodness and obedience.

﴿"In Him I have put my trust"﴾: I relied upon Him. ﴿"And to Him I turn in repentance"﴾: I return to Him in what befalls me of calamities. It was also said: this refers to the Return (to Allah) in the Hereafter.

﴿"And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you"﴾: let it not drive you, ﴿"that there befall you"﴾, meaning: because of doing what I forbid you from, ﴿"the like of what befell the people of Noah"﴾ of drowning, ﴿"or the people of Hud"﴾ of the wind, ﴿"or the people of Salih"﴾ of the blast. ﴿"And the people of Lut are not far from you."﴾ That is because they were close in time to the destruction of the people of Lut. [(In "B": "neighbours") of the people of Lut.]

[It was also said: the meaning is, "the land of the people of Lut is not far from you," because they were the neighbours of the people of Lut.]

﴿"And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving."﴾ "Al-Wadud" has two meanings: first, that He is loving toward the believers; and it was also said that it means "the one who is loved," i.e., the beloved of the believers. It has come in a report that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was the orator of the prophets, peace be upon them. [Mentioned by Abu al-Shaykh from Sufyan. See: Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani: 2/522.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 95–105:

﴿As though they had never prospered therein.﴾ That is, as though they had never dwelt there. ﴿Away with them! Just as Thamud was made away with.﴾ "Away" means destruction. ﴿For Madyan, just as Thamud was destroyed.﴾ ("Made away with" means destroyed.)

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We sent Musa with Our signs and a clear authority,﴾ meaning a manifest proof.

﴿To Fir'awn and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Fir'awn, and the command of Fir'awn was not rightly guided,﴾ meaning it was not sound.

﴿He will go before his people﴾ leading them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, and will bring them down﴾ meaning he will lead them into, ﴿the Fire. Wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought.﴾ That is, wretched is the place of entry and what is entered into.

﴿And they were followed by a curse in this [world], and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift that is given.﴾ That is, in this world, ﴿a curse﴾. "Wretched is the gift that is given" means the help that is helped, that is, the aid that is given. It is also said it means the reward that is bestowed, because the two curses followed one another upon them: a curse in this world and a curse in the Hereafter.

﴿That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you. Some of them still stand, and some are mown down.﴾ "Still stand" means inhabited, and "mown down" means ruined. It is also said: some of them still stand, meaning the walls remain while the roofs have fallen, and "mown down" means its trace has been effaced. Muqatil said: "still stand" means a trace of it can still be seen, and "mown down" means no trace of it can be seen. "Mown down" here means "reaped."

﴿And We did not wrong them,﴾ by the punishment and the destruction, ﴿but they wronged themselves,﴾ by disbelief and disobedience.

﴿So their gods, which they called upon besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came,﴾ meaning the punishment of your Lord. ﴿And they added nothing to them but ruin,﴾ that is, nothing but loss. It is also said it means destruction.

﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] related to us: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us: Yazid ibn Abi Burdah informed us, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then he recited: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing,﴾ and the verse.¹

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾ meaning a lesson ﴿for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection, and it is a Day witnessed by the people of the heavens and the earth.

﴿And We do not delay it﴾ meaning We do not delay that Day, so We do not establish the Resurrection upon you [for any reason] [and Ya'qub recited: "And He does not delay it," with the letter ya] ² ﴿except for a limited term,﴾ [known] ² with Allah.

﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be the wretched and the happy.﴾ "It comes" is recited with the letter ya and without it. "No soul will speak" means no soul will speak. "Among them will be the wretched and the happy" means among them are those for whom wretchedness has preceded, and among them are those for whom happiness has preceded.

Abu Sa'id Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather Abu Sahl Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Udhafiri informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abbad al-Dabari informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We went out to a funeral, and while we were at al-Baqi', the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us with a staff in his hand. He came and sat down, then he poked the ground with it for a while, then said: "There is no soul whose place has not been written, whether in Paradise or in the Fire, and it has been written either wretched or happy." A man said: "Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on our Decree and abandon action?" He said: "No, but act, for each is made easy for what he was created for. As for the people of wretchedness, they are made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness, and as for the people of happiness, they are made easy for the deeds of the people of happiness." Then he recited: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah] and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for him who is stingy and considers himself free of need and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship.﴾ [al-Layl: 5–10]³

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 106–107:

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, having therein groaning and wailing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: *al-zafir* is a loud sound, and *al-shahiq* is a weak sound. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: *al-zafir* is the beginning of a donkey's bray, and *al-shahiq* is its end, when it repeats it in its throat. Abu al-'Aliyah said: *al-zafir* is in the throat, and *al-shahiq* is in the chest.

﴿Abiding therein﴾: remaining and staying there. ﴿For as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "For as long as the heavens and earth of Paradise and Hell endure, and everything that is above you and shades you is a sky, and everything upon which your foot rests is earth."

The scholars of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: This is an expression for eternity according to the habit of the Arabs. They say, "I will not come to you as long as the heavens and the earth endure," and "such-and-such will not happen as long as the night and day alternate," meaning: never.

The Exalted said: ﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾.

Scholars differed regarding these two exceptions. Some of them said: the exception regarding the people of wretchedness refers to a group of believers whom Allah causes to enter the Fire for sins they committed, and then brings them out of it. Thus this exception is of a different category, because those who were brought out of the Fire are among the blessed, and Allah has excepted them from the total of the wretched. [In "B": (min al-ashqiya')]. This is like what was reported to us:

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hafs ibn 'Umar informed us: Hisham informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Some people will be touched by a scorching from the Fire because of sins they committed, as a punishment. Then Allah will admit them into Paradise by His grace and mercy, and they will be called 'the people of Jahannam.'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, Bab Sifat al-Jannah wa al-Nar: 11/416, and in al-Tawhid, Bab ma ja'a fi qawl Allah ta'ala: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers": 13/434, and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/183. "Safa'" from the Fire means blackness from the scorch of the Fire, or a mark from it.]

We were also informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Yahya informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan: Abu Raja' informed us: 'Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A people will come out of the Fire through the intercession of Muhammad, and they will enter Paradise and be called 'the Jahannamiyyun.'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in the previous place: 11/418, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/183–184.]

As for the exception regarding the people of happiness, it refers to the duration of their stay in the Fire before entering Paradise.

It was also said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ refers to both groups, concerning the length of their lifespan in this world and their detention in the *barzakh* (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection) between death and the Resurrection, before their arrival in Paradise or Hell. That is: they will abide eternally in Paradise or Hell, except for this measure.

It was also said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ means: other than what your Lord wills, [its meaning being: abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, other than what your Lord wills], [[omitted in (B)]] by way of an addition beyond the duration of the existence of the heavens and the earth, and that is eternal abiding therein. This is like saying: "I owe so-and-so a thousand, except two thousand," meaning: other than the two thousand that were previously mentioned.

It was also said: *illa* (except) here carries the meaning of *wa* (and), that is: your Lord has willed the eternal abiding of these in the Fire and those in Paradise. This is like His saying: ﴿So that the people will have no argument against you, except those who do wrong﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 150], meaning: and not those who do wrong.

It was also said: the meaning is: "Had your Lord willed, He would have brought them out of it, but He does not will it, since He has decreed for them eternal abiding."

Al-Farra' said: This exception is one that Allah has stated but will not carry out, like your saying, "By Allah, I will surely strike you, unless I see otherwise," while your resolve is to strike him.

[Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The most correct of the interpretations of this verse is the view we mentioned from Qatadah and al-Dahhak: that this exception concerns the people of monotheism among the major sinners, that He will admit them into the Fire to abide therein forever, except for what your Lord wills of their remaining there for less than that, after which He will bring them out and admit them into Paradise. We say this is the most correct view because Allah, the Majestic, threatened the people of polytheism with eternal abiding in the Fire, and reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confirm this. It is not permissible that this be an exception concerning the people of polytheism, and reports have been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Allah will admit some people of faith into the Fire for sins they committed, then bring them out and admit them into Paradise. It is not permissible that this be an exception concerning the people of monotheism before their entering it, given the soundness of the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that we have mentioned. And if we were to take it as an exception in this sense, we would have entered into the view of those who say: "No sinner enters Paradise, and no believer enters the Fire," and that contradicts the position of the people of knowledge and what the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) have brought. When these two interpretations are invalid, there remains no view held by the leading scholars except the third, which is the preferred one. See al-Tabari: 15/484–485.]

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of whatever He wills﴾.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 106–107:

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, having therein groaning and wailing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: *al-zafir* is a loud sound, and *al-shahiq* is a weak sound. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: *al-zafir* is the beginning of a donkey's bray, and *al-shahiq* is its end, when it repeats it in its throat. Abu al-'Aliyah said: *al-zafir* is in the throat, and *al-shahiq* is in the chest.

﴿Abiding therein﴾: remaining and staying there. ﴿For as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "For as long as the heavens and earth of Paradise and Hell endure, and everything that is above you and shades you is a sky, and everything upon which your foot rests is earth."

The scholars of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: This is an expression for eternity according to the habit of the Arabs. They say, "I will not come to you as long as the heavens and the earth endure," and "such-and-such will not happen as long as the night and day alternate," meaning: never.

The Exalted said: ﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾.

Scholars differed regarding these two exceptions. Some of them said: the exception regarding the people of wretchedness refers to a group of believers whom Allah causes to enter the Fire for sins they committed, and then brings them out of it. Thus this exception is of a different category, because those who were brought out of the Fire are among the blessed, and Allah has excepted them from the total of the wretched. [In "B": (min al-ashqiya')]. This is like what was reported to us:

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hafs ibn 'Umar informed us: Hisham informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Some people will be touched by a scorching from the Fire because of sins they committed, as a punishment. Then Allah will admit them into Paradise by His grace and mercy, and they will be called 'the people of Jahannam.'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, Bab Sifat al-Jannah wa al-Nar: 11/416, and in al-Tawhid, Bab ma ja'a fi qawl Allah ta'ala: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers": 13/434, and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/183. "Safa'" from the Fire means blackness from the scorch of the Fire, or a mark from it.]

We were also informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Yahya informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan: Abu Raja' informed us: 'Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A people will come out of the Fire through the intercession of Muhammad, and they will enter Paradise and be called 'the Jahannamiyyun.'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in the previous place: 11/418, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/183–184.]

When these two interpretations are invalid, there remains no view held by the leading scholars except the third, which is the preferred one. See al-Tabari: 15/484–485.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 108:

﴿And as for those who were made happy﴾ Ḥamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ḥafs read ﴿suʻidū﴾ with a ḍammah on the sīn [and a kasrah on the ʻayn], meaning: they were granted happiness (saʻādah). Su'ida and Ut'ida have the same meaning. The others read it with a fatḥah on the sīn, by analogy with "shaqū" (they were made wretched).

﴿Then in the Garden they will abide therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾ Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "except for the time they remained in the Fire until they were admitted into the Garden." Qatadah said: "God knows best its exception (thunyāh)."

﴿A gift without cutting off﴾ meaning, not cut off. Ibn Zayd said: "God the Exalted informed us about what He wills for the people of the Garden when He said: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, but He did not inform us about what He wills for the people of the Fire."

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "There will come a time upon Hell when no one will be in it, and that is after they have remained in it for ages (aḥqāb)." [[See: Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani: 2/527.]]

And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, the like of it. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/478. See also: Fath al-Qadir, same place, where al-Shawkani refutes al-Zamakhshari.]]

Its meaning according to the People of the Sunnah, if it is established, is that no one of the people of faith will remain in it. As for the places of the disbelievers, they will be filled forever.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 11, verses 109–111:

﴿So do not be in doubt﴾ (in shakk, "doubt"), ﴿about what these worship﴾ (that they are misguided). ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before﴾: there is an omitted element (idmar) here, meaning "as their fathers used to worship." ﴿And indeed, We will give them their share﴾, their portion of the recompense, ﴿in full﴾.

﴿Without reduction﴾.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿but it was disputed about﴾, so some believed in it and some denied it, just as your people did with the Qur'an. He consoles his Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord﴾ concerning the delay of the punishment for them, ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, meaning they would have been punished immediately, and their punishment and destruction would have been settled. ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt about it﴾, meaning a doubt that causes suspicion and accusation.

﴿And indeed, all﴾: Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Bakr read "wa-in kullan" with the nun silent, as a lightening of the heavy inna. The rest read it with the shaddah. ﴿Lamma﴾: Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Hamzah read it with the shaddah here and in Ya-Sin and at-Tariq. Abu Ja'far agreed with them here and in at-Tariq and az-Zukhruf in reading it with the shaddah, as did 'Asim and Hamzah [[The text in parentheses is missing from "ب".]]. The rest read it without the shaddah. Whoever reads it with the shaddah says: the original form is ﴿wa-inna kullan﴾ [la-min ma], then the preposition min was joined to ma, so the nun was changed into a mim for assimilation. Three mims then came together and one of them was deleted, leaving lamma with the shaddah. Here "ma" has the meaning of "man" (whoever), a term for a group of people, as God Most High says: ﴿marry what seems good to you﴾ [an-Nisa: 3], meaning "those who seem good to you." The meaning is: ﴿And indeed, all﴾ are from a group that ﴿your Lord will certainly compensate [in full]﴾ [[The text in parentheses is missing from "ب".]].

Whoever reads it without the shaddah says: "ma" is a superfluous particle (silah), [inserted between the two lams so that they are separated, because of the dislike of their coming together. The meaning is] [[The text in parentheses is missing from "ب".]] ﴿And indeed, all, He will surely compensate them﴾.

It is also said that "ma" means "min," its implied form being: la-min la-yuwaffiyannahum. The lam in "lamma" is the lam of emphasis [which enters upon the predicate of inna] [[The text in parentheses is missing from "ب".]], and the lam in "la-yuwaffiyannahum" is the lam of oath, [and the oath is implied] [[The text in parentheses is missing from "ب".]], its implied form being: "By God." ﴿Your Lord will certainly compensate them for their deeds﴾, meaning the recompense for their deeds. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verses 112–113:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾, meaning: be steadfast in the religion of your Lord, in acting upon it, and in calling to it, as you have been commanded. ﴿And those who turn with you﴾, meaning: those who believe with you, let them also be steadfast. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Steadfastness (istiqamah) is that you remain upright in obeying the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, and that you do not swerve away like a fox's swerving." [[Attributed in Kanz al-ʿUmmal (2/495) to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim, Ibn al-Mundhir, Rustah in al-Iman, and al-Sabuni in al-Mi'atayn.]]

It was narrated to us by the Imam al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi: Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: my father informed us by dictation: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla' ibn Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from Sufyan ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying about Islam about which I will not have to ask anyone after you." He said: "Say: 'I have believed in Allah,' then be steadfast." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the comprehensive characteristics of Islam, no. (38): 1/65, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/31.]]

﴿And do not transgress﴾: do not go beyond My command, and do not disobey Me. It was also said: its meaning is "do not exaggerate, so that you add to what I have commanded and prohibited."

﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾: nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "No verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that was harder on him than this verse, and for this reason he said: 'Hud and its sister surahs have turned my hair gray.'" [[This will be cited shortly at the end of the surah.]]

It was narrated to us by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Malihi: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from Maʿn ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, the religion is ease, and no one makes the religion difficult except that it overcomes him. So aim for correctness, come close to it, rejoice, and seek help through the morning, the evening, and a portion of the night." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "The religion is ease": 1/93, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/49–50. Al-Dulja: it is travel in the last part of the night, and it was said: the whole night.]]

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Do not lean toward them." Al-Rukun is love and inclination of the heart. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: "Do not be pleased with their deeds." al-Suddi said: "Do not flatter the wrongdoers." It is narrated from ʿIkrimah: "Do not obey them." It was also said: "Do not settle down with those who have done wrong."

﴿Lest the Fire touch you﴾, meaning: lest it afflict you, ﴿and you have no protectors other than Allah﴾, meaning: no helpers who can shield you from His punishment, ﴿then you would not be helped﴾.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Do not lean toward them." Al-Rukun is love and inclination of the heart. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: "Do not be pleased with their deeds." al-Suddi said: "Do not flatter the wrongdoers." It is narrated from ʿIkrimah: "Do not obey them." It was also said: "Do not settle down with those who have done wrong."

﴿Lest the Fire touch you﴾, meaning: lest it afflict you, ﴿and you have no protectors other than Allah﴾, meaning: no helpers who can shield you from His punishment, ﴿then you would not be helped﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 114:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, i.e., the morning (al-ghadah) and the evening (al-ʿashiyy). [That is: the Dawn prayer and the Maghrib prayer.] Mujahid said: "The two ends of the day are the prayer of the Dawn [prayer], the Dhuhr and the ʿAsr." ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾: the Maghrib prayer and the ʿIsha' prayer.

Muqatil said: The Fajr and Dhuhr prayers are one end, and the ʿAsr and Maghrib prayers are the other end. ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾ means the ʿIsha' prayer.

Al-Hasan said: "The two ends of the day": the Subh (dawn) and the ʿAsr. ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾: the Maghrib and the ʿIsha'. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The two ends of the day are al-ghadah and al-ʿashiyy," meaning the Dawn prayer and the Maghrib prayer.

His saying: ﴿And at the approaches of the night﴾, i.e., its hours; its singular is zulfah (zulfah). Abu Jaʿfar recited "zulufan" with a damma on the lam.

﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, meaning: indeed, the five prayers remove sins.

It is narrated that it was revealed concerning Abu al-Yasar, who said: A woman came to me to buy dates, and I said to her: "In the house there are dates better than these." So she entered the house with me, and I leaned toward her and kissed her. Then I came to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Conceal your sin and repent." Then I came to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Conceal your sin and repent." But I could not be patient, so I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said: "Have you wronged a man who fights in the cause of Allah, left behind in his family, with the like of this, until he thought he was among the people of the Fire?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head until Allah revealed to him: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾ up to the end of the verse. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is this for him specifically or for people in general?" He said: "Rather, it is for people in general." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surah Hud, from Abu al-Yasar: 8/538-539, and he said: this is a hasan sahih gharib hadith... and on the subject there are reports from Abu Umamah, Wathilah ibn al-Asqa, and Anas ibn Malik. Abu al-Yasar's name is Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr. It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Tabarani and al-Tabari. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/482; Fath al-Bari: 8/356; al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 88; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi pp. 306-310.]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu ʿUthman al-Nahdi, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man had kissed a woman, so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for me?" He said: "It is for all of my nation, all of them." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the tafsir, Surah Hud, chapter "And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day..." 8/355.]

And Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Abu Tahir and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Aili told me, both said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr, that ʿUmar ibn Ishaq, the client of Za'idah, narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "The five prayers, and the Friday from one Friday to the next, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, provided major sins are avoided." [Narrated by Muslim in Taharah, chapter on the five prayers and Friday to Friday..., no. (233): 1/209, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/177.]

And ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Makhaldi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Qutaybah informed us: al-Layth and Bakr ibn Mudar informed us, from Ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you think, if there were a river at the door of one of you in which he bathed five times every day, would any of its filth remain on him?" They said: "No." He said: "That is the likeness of the five prayers; Allah wipes out sins through them." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Times of Prayer, chapter "The five prayers are an expiation": 2/11, and Muslim in the Book of Mosques, chapter "Walking to prayer erases sins," no. (667): 1/462-463. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/175.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿That﴾, i.e., that which we have mentioned. It was also said: it refers to the Qur'an. ﴿A reminder﴾, an admonition ﴿for those who remember﴾, i.e., for those who remember it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 11, verse 115:

﴿And be patient﴾, O Muhammad, over what you suffer of harm. It is also said: "over the prayer." A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good﴾ in their deeds. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "It means those who pray."

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Why then were there not﴾ (fahallā), among the generations that We destroyed ﴿before you﴾, ﴿those possessing a remnant﴾ (ūlū baqiyyah). The verse is a rebuke. ﴿Possessing a remnant﴾ means possessing discernment (tamyīz). It is also said: possessing obedience. And it is said: possessing goodness. It is said, "So-and-so is one of remnant (dhū baqiyyah)" when there is goodness in him. The meaning is: Why were there not, among the generations before you, people with goodness who forbade corruption on the earth?

[And it is said: the meaning is "possessing a remnant of goodness." It is said, "So-and-so is upon a remnant of goodness" when he is upon a praiseworthy quality.] [[Omitted in manuscript "B".]]

﴿Who forbade corruption on the earth﴾, that is, who stood up to forbid corruption. Its meaning is also "denied": that is, there were no people of remnant among them.

﴿Except a few﴾: this is a disjunctive exception (istithnā' munqati'), meaning: "But a few," ﴿of those whom We saved from among them﴾, and they are the followers of the prophets, who used to forbid corruption on the earth.

﴿But those who did wrong pursued what they were given of luxury﴾, that is, what they were made to enjoy (nu'{{ima}}), ﴿therein﴾. The mutraf is the one who is given comfort. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: they were given provisions (khuwwilū). Al-Farra' said: [they were habituated to comfort, pleasures, and preference for this world]. [[Omitted in manuscript "B".]] That is: those who did wrong pursued what they had been habituated to of comfort, pleasures, and preferring this world over the Hereafter.

﴿And they were criminals﴾, that is, disbelievers.

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, that is, He does not destroy them for their polytheism, ﴿while their people were reformers﴾ among themselves, dealing justly and not wronging one another. He destroys them only when they wrong one another. It is also said: He does not destroy them through an injustice from Him while they are doing good in their deeds. Rather, He destroys them for their disbelief and their committing evil deeds.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind﴾ all of them ﴿one community﴾ upon one religion.

﴿And they will not cease to be in disagreement﴾ over diverse religions, among them Jews, Christians, Magians, and polytheists.

﴿Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾. Its meaning: But those upon whom your Lord has mercy, so He guides them to the truth; they do not differ. ﴿And for that He created them﴾. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: and for disagreement He created them. Ashhab said: I asked Malik about this verse, and he said: He created them so that there would be a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

Abu 'Ubayda said: What I choose is the view of the one who said: He created one party for His mercy and one party for His punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: And for mercy He created them, meaning those whom He has shown mercy to.

Al-Farra' said: He created the people of mercy for mercy, and the people of disagreement for disagreement.

The summary of the verse is: the people of falsehood disagree, and the people of truth agree. So God created the people of truth for agreement, and the people of falsehood for disagreement.

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, that is, the decree of your Lord has been fulfilled: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾

We were informed by Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Jawzajani: Abu al-Qasim ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi related to us: Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla' related to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham related to us, from Shayban, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown gray." So the Prophet ﷺ said: "Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, ʿAmma yatasa'alun, and Idha al-shamsu kuwwirat have made me gray."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the commentary on Surat al-Waqi'ah: 9/184, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas except through this route." See: al-Matalib al-ʿAliyah: 3/342, al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 87, Fayd al-Qadir of al-Munawi: 4/168, and Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/37.]]
